name: VA-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Jennifer McClellan running for reelection
Minimal Republican fundraising and no outside spending
Prediction markets price Democratic win near certain
model.rationale: A D+17 district with a well-funded incumbent and no competitive polling or spending to suggest movement leaves little basis to depart from fundamentals; Polymarket also prices McClellan near certain.
model.watch: Any late independent polling or unexpected outside spending against McClellan would be the first sign of movement in this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Virginia's 4th District is a strongly Democratic seat, with a partisan lean of about 17 points toward Democrats. Jennifer McClellan, the Democratic incumbent, is running for reelection after winning the seat comfortably and has raised over $1.1 million for the campaign. Her Republican opponent, Robert Murray, has reported no fundraising figures, and there is no outside spending on either side.

No public general-election polls cover the race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets give McClellan roughly a 97 percent chance of winning. With the fundamentals, money, and market pricing all pointing the same direction, this race is rated Safe Democratic, with McClellan expected to win by a wide margin.
